title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Cooper Rush released by Falcons
items.desc: The Falcons released QB Cooper Rush.
items.impact: Rush struggled to begin the season as the Falcons starter. Atlanta signed Andy Dalton as the corresponding move.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Andy Dalton signs with Falcons
items.desc: The Falcons signed QB Andy Dalton.
items.impact: Dalton was recently released by the Eagles. He could compete with Tua Tagovailoa to backup Michael Penix Jr.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Elijah Arroyo (shoulder) to likely be placed on IR
items.desc: Elijah Arroyo is expected to be placed on injured reserve.
items.impact: Arroyo is expected to miss an extended period of time. He'll miss at least four weeks if/when he is placed on injured reserve.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Monroe Freeling (knee) could return in Week 7
items.desc: Monroe Freeling could return in Week 7 against the Buccaneers.
items.impact: "This is a first-round pick for us but we're gonna do what's best for the Panthers," Panthers coach Dave Canales said. Freeling will need to be monitored in practice throughout the week.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Jalon Daniels starter status up in the air Mayfield returning
items.desc: Jalon Daniels is starting off practice on Wednesday as the presumed starter, at least for initial game planning, for Week 7. Baker Mayfield is set to return to practice, and his performance will likely determine which of the two will end up being named the starter against Carolina.
items.impact: If Mayfield shows enough spark throughout the weeks and few ill effects from his injury, Mayfield will likely start unless the Bucs show an abundance of caution and start Daniels anyway. If Baker can't go, Daniels has shown decent enough ability when rushing to at least give him a floor, but lacks much of a ceiling due to little passing production in each of his three starts.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Baker Mayfield (thumb) set to practice on Wednesday
items.desc: Baker Mayfield (thumb) is set to practice on Wednesday to test his health for Week 7's contest against Carolina.
items.impact: While Mayfield is expected to start practicing, the team is still planning as if Jalon Daniels will start in Week 7, which isn't surprising given the situation. If Mayfield is healthy enough to start, then he will likely lead the team against the Panthers and be a low-end QB2 for fantasy.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Sauce Gardner (calf) expected to miss time with calf strain
items.desc: Sauce Gardner (calf) is expected to miss time with a calf strain and is labeled week-to-week. However, he's not expected to miss an extended period.
items.impact: Gardner was unable to finish the Colts game against the Titans due to the injury. It's tough blow to an already struggling secondary, but it's not as if Gardner is wasn't part of the problem.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Raiders D/ST struggles in loss Sunday
items.desc: The Raiders' D/ST logged two sacks and allowed 33 points in Sunday's loss to the Buffalo Bills.
items.impact: Las Vegas' defense was outmatched on Sunday. They allowed Buffalo's offense to score 33 points over the course of the afternoon, and they weren't able to log any big plays to help turn the tide of the game. This unit shouldn't be started moving forward, even in favorable matchups.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Matt Gay scores 12 points in loss Sunday
items.desc: Matt Gay went 3-for-3 on his field-goal attempts and 3-for-3 on his extra-point attempts in Sunday's 33-30 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
items.impact: Gay did his job on Sunday, knocking down all six of his attempted kicks in Las Vegas' narrow loss to the Buffalo Bills. Fantasy managers should be happy with his performance and should continue to view him as a decent fantasy option at the position moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Dylan Laube uninvolved in loss Sunday
items.desc: Dylan Laube rushed the ball one time for zero yards and caught one pass for -1 yards in Sunday's 33-30 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
items.impact: Laube was able to play on Sunday but didn't do much against the Bills. He saw just two touches and finished with negative yards in this matchup. He is clearly eclipsed by Mike Washington Jr. on the depth chart at this point, so he will be irrelevant from a fantasy perspective moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jalen Nailor quiet in loss Sunday
items.desc: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-4 targets for nine yards in Sunday's 33-30 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
items.impact: Nailor wasn't able to do much on Sunday. He caught just one pass over the course of the game and was only able to turn that into nine yards, which left him with a terrible fantasy total. Fantasy managers shouldn't have high expectations for him moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Michael Mayer hauls in seven passes Sunday
items.desc: Michael Mayer hauled in 7-of-9 targets for 95 yards in Sunday's 33-30 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
items.impact: Mayer had a great performance on Sunday. He set a new career high in receiving yards against the Bills, racking up 95 on his seven catches, which left him with a great fantasy total. He may have some good games here or there moving forward, but he's unlikely to be a reliable week-to-week asset with TE Brock Bowers still easily ahead of him in the pecking order at this point.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Mike Washington Jr. leads team in rushing Sunday
items.desc: Mike Washington Jr. rushed the ball nine times for 43 yards and caught one pass for seven yards in Sunday's 33-30 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
items.impact: Washington was surprisingly involved on Sunday. He saw just one less carry than Ashton Jeanty over the course of the afternoon, and he was much more efficient with his work, leading the team in rushing yards at an efficient clip of 4.8 yards per carry as opposed to Jeanty's 2.2 yards per carry. Washington may be earning more touches for himself moving forward, which would be bad news for the fantasy value of Jeanty.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tre Tucker stellar in loss Sunday
items.desc: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-7 targets for 97 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 33-30 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
items.impact: Tucker had a stellar performance on Sunday. He led the team with 97 yards over the course of the afternoon and he was also able to get into the end zone on two occasions, which left him with a great fantasy total on the day. Fantasy managers should consider picking him up if he's available on the waiver wire, as the team may very well try to get him more involved on a week-to-week basis after this game.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Brock Bowers solid in loss Sunday
items.desc: Brock Bowers caught 4-of-9 targets for 70 yards in Sunday's 33-30 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
items.impact: Bowers had a solid fantasy finish on Sunday, but his performance was slightly disappointing, since he was only able to haul in four of his nine targets over the course of a shootout game. He should continue to be a top-tier fantasy option moving forward, even with a slightly less impressive performance in this game than usual.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Ashton Jeanty inefficient in loss Sunday
items.desc: Ashton Jeanty rushed the ball ten times for 22 yards and a touchdown and caught 4-of-6 targets for 36 yards in Sunday's 33-30 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
items.impact: Jeanty ended up having a decent fantasy outing on Sunday between his involvement in the receiving game and his touchdown on the ground. But he was very inefficient on the ground, rushing at a clip of just 2.2 yards per carry, and finished with less rushing yards than Mike Washington Jr., who was more involved than expected again Buffalo. Fantasy managers should continue to monitor Jeanty moving forward, especially to see if he's still dealing with any nagging injuries at this point.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kirk Cousins throws two touchdowns in loss Sunday
items.desc: Kirk Cousins completed 23-of-41 passing attempts for 313 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in Sunday's 33-30 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
items.impact: Cousins played a pretty good game on Sunday. His interception was a blemish, but besides that he threw for over 300 yards and two touchdowns in a narrow loss to the Bills. He has been playing quite well lately and will continue to be a worthwhile streaming option moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Bills D/ST dismal in win Sunday
items.desc: The Bills' D/ST logged one interception and allowed 30 points in Sunday's win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: Buffalo's defense looked terrible again in Week 6. They allowed Las Vegas to score 30 points over the course of the game, and they weren't able to log a single sack or turnover beyond one interception to help out their offense. This unit has been very bad to start the year and should not be started in any matchups for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tyler Bass scores 15 points in win Sunday
items.desc: Tyler Bass went 4-for-4 on his field-goal attempts and 3-for-3 on his extra-point attempts in Sunday's 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: Bass played quite well on Sunday. He made all seven of his kicks and was responsible for 15 of Buffalo's points on the afternoon, which made a big impact in a game that they won by just three points. He will continue to be a good option at the kicker position for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Joshua Palmer catches one pass in win Sunday
items.desc: Joshua Palmer caught 1-of-2 targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: The veteran wideout wasn't very involved on Sunday, but he was still able to make his mark with one 37-yard catch on the afternoon. He remains irrelevant for fantasy purposes at this point, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Dawson Knox silent in win Sunday
items.desc: Dawson Knox caught one pass for zero yards in Sunday's 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: The veteran didn't do much on Sunday, recording zero yards on just one catch over the course of the game. He remains off of the fantasy radar entirely for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Khalil Shakir finds end zone Sunday
items.desc: Khalil Shakir caught 4-of-6 targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: Shakir was a bit disappointing as far as yardage goes on Sunday, but he made up for that by scoring one of Buffalo's touchdowns through the air. Still, he isn't a reliable fantasy option at this point, and fantasy managers should be especially wary about starting him whenever DJ Moore (shoulder) is back in the lineup for Buffalo.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Keon Coleman leads team in receiving Sunday
items.desc: Keon Coleman caught 4-of-6 targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: Coleman stepped up with DJ Moore (shoulder) sidelined for the Bills on Sunday. He led the team with 59 receiving yards against the Raiders, and he was also able to get into the end zone at one point, which left him with a nice fantasy total on the day. He should continue to be started in most league formats if Moore has to miss additional time beyond this game.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Dalton Kincaid hauls in seven passes Sunday
items.desc: Dalton Kincaid hauled on 7-of-8 passing attempts for 38 yards in Sunday's 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: Kincaid saw a lot of involvement on Sunday, leading the team with eight targets and seven catches in a win over the Raiders. He wasn't able to do much with his work, however, racking up just 38 scoreless yards over the course of the game. It's encouraging to see them take pains to get him involved, but it's still hard to trust starting him in most fantasy formats at this point in the season.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Jalen Hurts (blood clot) out for the season as additional clots are found
items.desc: Jalen Hurts (blood clot) is out for the remainder of the 2026 NFL Season due to blood clots found in his lungs. Hurts was on blood thinners already to treat the clot that was originally found, but will need additional treatment to bring him back to full health. He is expected to make a full recovery.
items.impact: A report by Rapoport noted Hurts played in London with no sleep, as sleep was a risk for the QB. This is obviously extremely serious news for Hurts, his family, and the team, so don't lose sight of that, but it's relieving to hear he should make a full recovery. As for football, it's a big blow for an already struggling Eagles team, who will now proceed with Tanner McKee at QB. Don't be surprised if Cole Payton also sees some run towards the end of the year if things really fly south for the Eagles.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: James Cook III plays well in win Sunday
items.desc: James Cook III rushed the ball 22 times for 95 yards and a touchdown and caught three passes for 58 yards in Sunday's 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: Cook played great on Sunday. He finished with over 150 total yards and a touchdown against the Raiders, which helped to lead the Bills to a big win on the road. He should continue to be a top-tier fantasy asset for as long as he remains healthy and on the field moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Josh Allen scores twice in win Sunday
items.desc: Josh Allen completed 23-of-33 passing attempts for 255 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 33-30 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: Allen played a solid game on Sunday, racking up 255 yards and two touchdowns through the air while not turning the ball over at all. He had just one yard on the ground in this game, however, which is extremely uncommon for him, especially after he rushed for over 120 yards last week. Fantasy managers should continue to view him as a top-tier fantasy option moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Rams D/ST allows 18 points in loss Sunday
items.desc: The Rams' D/ST logged one interception and allowed 18 points in Sunday's loss to the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: Los Angeles' defense wasn't good on Sunday. They held Arizona's offense to just 18 points, but they were held to just one forced turnover and didn't log even a single sack over the course of the game, which didn't help their own offense. This unit has an easier schedule over the next couple of weeks, but it will still be hard to trust starting them from a fantasy perspective.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Blake Grupe suffers injury in loss Sunday
items.desc: Blake Grupe made his lone field-goal attempt before suffering an injury and leaving Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: The Rams just brought in Grupe to replace the recently-cut Harrison Mevis, but he suffered an injury in his first game as a Ram after taking a big hit on a kickoff. It seems likely that he is going to miss time, which will leave Los Angeles looking for a new kicker before next week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Colby Parkinson hauls in touchdown Sunday
items.desc: Colby Parkinson hauled in 5-of-6 targets for 31 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: The veteran was a bright spot for the Rams on Sunday. He was able to catch one of their two touchdowns over the course of the afternoon, but they still suffered an ugly loss at the hands of the Cardinals. Fantasy managers shouldn't be expecting him to produce in a consistent manner moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tyler Higbee catches four passes Sunday
items.desc: Tyler Higbee caught four passes for 22 yards in Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: Higbee caught four passes over the course of the afternoon on Sunday, but he wasn't able to do much with them, racking up just 22 yards in a loss to the Cardinals. Fantasy managers shouldn't have high expectations for him moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Blake Corum scores once in loss Sunday
items.desc: Blake Corum rushed the ball nine times for 42 yards and caught two passes for 18 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: Corum got involved on Sunday, seeing 11 total touches in the team's loss to the Cardinals. He was able to get into the end zone on one of his catches, but he still didn't end up with more than just a solid fantasy total. He will likely continue to serve as an involved RB2 behind Kyren Williams moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Davante Adams suffers leg injury in loss Sunday
items.desc: Davante Adams caught 3-of-4 targets for 39 yards before leaving Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals early with a leg injury of some kind.
items.impact: Adams wasn't having a good game late on Sunday, and things got worse when he suffered a lower-body injury of some kind late in the game. Los Angeles wasn't able to pick up the win, and fantasy managers should keep very close tabs on all updates about his health throughout the week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Puka Nacua leads team in receiving Sunday
items.desc: Puka Nacua hauled in 6-of-7 targets for 80 yards in Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: Nacua was a bright spot for the Rams on Sunday. He led the team with 80 yards over the course of the day, though he wasn't able to get into the end zone at all to put the cherry on top. Still, fantasy managers should be content with his performance and should expect him to continue to be an elite fantasy asset moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kyren Williams leads team in rushing Sunday
items.desc: Kyren Williams rushed the ball ten times for 50 yards and caught 3-of-6 targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: Williams saw 16 opportunities on Sunday, but he was a bit disappointing with them, racking up 67 yards without a touchdown in the team's loss to the Cardinals. After the game he voiced some frustrations about the timeshare the team currently has in the backfield, but fantasy managers shouldn't be too concerned about him moving forward and should continue to start him without reservation for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Matthew Stafford throws two touchdowns in loss Sunday
items.desc: Matthew Stafford completed 25-of-33 passing attempts for 222 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: Stafford looked pretty good on Sunday. He threw for over 200 yards and two touchdowns over the course of the afternoon, but that wasn't enough for the Rams, as they still put up just 16 points and suffered a loss at the hands of the Cardinals. Stafford should continue to be a relevant fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cardinals D/ST allows 16 points Sunday
items.desc: The Cardinals' D/ST logged two sacks and a fumble recovery while allowing just 16 points in Sunday's upset win over the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Arizona's defense played a great game on Sunday. They allowed just 16 points to one of the league's most potent offenses, which led to the Cardinals picking up a stunning upset win on the road. Despite the good performance, they should not be started for fantasy purposes moving forward, even in favorable matchups.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Chad Ryland scores 18 points in win Sunday
items.desc: Chad Ryland went 6-for-6 on his field-goal attempts in Sunday's 18-16 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Ryland was terrific on Sunday. He scored all 18 of Arizona's points in their upset win over the Rams and made the game-winning kick under pressure at the end of the game. He should continue to be a worthwhile fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Elijah Higgins catches three passes Sunday
items.desc: Elijah Higgins caught three passes for 28 yards in Sunday's 18-16 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Higgins has proven to be a useful role player for the Cardinals recently, and that continued on Sunday, when he caught three passes in the team's upset win over the Rams. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to be worth picking up anytime soon, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jalen Brooks solid in win Sunday
items.desc: Jalen Brooks caught 2-of-3 targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 18-16 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Brooks was able to contribute on Sunday, catching two passes for 30 yards in the team's win over the Rams. He doesn't currently see enough work to be a relevant fantasy option for the foreseeable future, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Bam Knight leads team in rushing Sunday
items.desc: Bam Knight rushed the ball 15 times for 80 yards and caught two passes for 18 yards in Sunday's 18-16 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Knight stepped up on Sunday with rookie Jeremiyah Love (ankle) out of the lineup for Arizona. He was able to churn out 98 total yards over the course of the afternoon while maintaining an efficient clip of 5.3 yards per carry on the ground. He won't continue to be relevant when Love is able to make his return to the lineup in the near future, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kendrick Bourne racks up 47 yards Sunday
items.desc: Kendrick Bourne hauled in 5-of-8 targets for 47 yards in Sunday's 18-16 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: The veteran wideout was productive enough on Sunday. Bourne was able to rack up 47 yards on his five receptions, though he failed to score a touchdown with that, which led to a subpar fantasy total for him. He should continue to have respectable fantasy value as a streaming option for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tyler Allgeier inefficient in win Sunday
items.desc: Tyler Allgeier rushed the ball 18 times for 38 yards and caught one pass for ten yards in Sunday's 18-16 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Allgeier didn't look great on Sunday. He was projected to be a good fantasy option in the absence of rookie Jeremiyah Love (ankle), but he was only able to churn out 48 total yards on 20 opportunities. His efficiency continues to be his downfall, and fantasy managers shouldn't have too much hope that he will have significant value at any point this season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Michael Wilson held to 32 yards Sunday
items.desc: Michael Wilson caught 4-of-7 targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 18-16 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Wilson had a disappointing performance on Sunday. He saw plenty of opportunities with seven targets on the day, but he failed to capitalize on them and ended with just 32 yards in total. Fantasy managers should expect him to bounce back and perform better than this in the very near future, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Trey McBride leads team in receiving Sunday
items.desc: Trey McBride hauled in 7-of-9 targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 18-16 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: McBride continues to produce well in PPR scoring formats, hauling in seven passes in Sunday's upset win over the Rams. He wasn't able to turn those seven catches into much, but fantasy managers should still be satisfied with the performance that he put up.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jacoby Brissett scoreless in win Sunday
items.desc: Jacoby Brissett completed 24-of-35 passing attempts for 218 yards and one interception in Sunday's 18-16 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: The Cardinals were able to pick up a stunning win over the Rams on the road on Sunday, but that didn't have a lot to do with Brissett's performance. He didn't throw a touchdown in this game, and in fact, he didn't even lead the offense to a single touchdown over the course of the afternoon. He should continue to be an okay streaming option some weeks but shouldn't be trusted as much more than that.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Packers D/ST picks up two interceptions in Week 6
items.desc: The Packers D/ST allowed 13 points while notching two interceptions and one sack in a 23-13 win over the Cowboys in Week 6.
items.impact: Green Bay's defense was solid in the win, holding Dallas scoreless in the first half. They got interceptions from Evan Williams and Brandon Cisse while Lukas Van Ness provided the sack. The Packers will take on the Lions in Week 7.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Trey Smack hits three FGs in Week 6
items.desc: Trey Smack made all three of his field goals while adding two extra points in a 23-13 win over the Cowboys in Week 6.
items.impact: Smack hit field goals from 25, 44, and 29 yards out to help propel the Packers to the win over Dallas. The rookie has now made 10 of his 13 field-goal attempts while hitting 11 extra points this year. He will take on the Lions in Week 7.

items.author: Matthew Adam
items.title: Tucker Kraft catches five passes in Week 6
items.desc: Tucker Kraft caught five of his eight targets for 37 yards in a 23-13 win over the Cowboys in Week 6.
items.impact: Kraft finished tied for second on the team in targets but was able to manage just 37 yards in the win. The veteran tight end now has 25 catches for 249 yards and one touchdown in six games for the Packers this year. He will be a strong TE1 in Week 7 vs. the Lions.
